transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-27
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Nimbus CTO), Raj Patel (Nimbus Lead ML Eng), Alicia Gomez (Nimbus PM)

Auto-summary: quick console tour of Optimize > QProfiles, walk through an example INT8 and FP8 profile, show fidelity snapshots and latency heatmap, discuss guardrails and telemetry.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in, im samira from redwood, this should be a hands-on walkthrough of the optimize console qprofile flows - if we get into deep perf numbers ethan will take over
[00:18] Maya: thanks samira, excited, we flagged this as high priority because any small drift in clinical summaries could be a blocker, we need near-parity with our current float32 baseline
[00:32] Raj: just to state constraints up front, 99% of our requests need to return under 200ms tail latency, cost sensitivity matters but quality is priority, and we have to keep PII off the service or use KMS - we need to see how private deployment or VPC options look
[00:47] Ethan: great — we'll show both hosted and private guardrails, and how qprofiles let you express per-route tolerances. first quick tour of the console: QProfiles tab, snapshot view, fidelity heatmaps, and the sandbox runner
[01:12] Alicia: quick question — do qprofiles ship with model-specific presets or do we create from scratch?
[01:20] Ethan: good Q. we include curated presets for common families, but the right pattern is to start with a fidelity sweep using your prompts and then lock in a production profile. presets speed things up but we always recommend a small calibration run
[01:39] Samira: to orient numbers, our float32 baseline for the med-large model on our hosted infra is about 45ms median per token, and FP8 gives about 25-30% speedup vs float, INT8 typically give 40-60% speedup depending on kernel and sequence length — but there are nuance caveats on quality
[02:05] Raj: those percentages sound optimistic — can you show raw numbers for 1k prompt set? we need to know expected tail impact, not just median
[02:18] Ethan: absolutely, i pulled a quick sandbox run earlier with a 1k sample from your anonymized set — float baseline end-to-end median 42ms token, 95th 190ms; FP8 median 29ms token 95th 130ms; INT8 median 20ms token 95th 160ms — for some long context cases INT8 tail can widen because of quantization sensitivity, that's predictable from our sensitivity scans
[03:01] Maya: interesting, so FP8 reduces tail substantially and INT8 has lower median but sometimes worse tail? that pattern worries us because we have worst-case SLA concerns
[03:17] Ethan: right, that's where the QProfile runtime fallback comes in — you can express a rule: prefer INT8 for cost, but if runtime sampling detects degraded probs on key prompts, automatically route those specific prompts to FP8 or float for that route. automatic rollbacks are also an option if eval metrics cross a threshold
[03:40] Raj: how do you detect 'degraded probs'? we need something deterministic — we can't rely on soft heuristics for clinical correctness
[03:49] Ethan: good point — we use a mix: prompt-level evals (expected-token-probs, perplexity delta vs baseline), task-specific metrics (e.g., ROUGE for summaries), and cached reference prompts that run through a small regression set each minute. thresholds are configurable in the console per-route
[04:12] Samira: i'll pull up the telemetry tab — here's an example fidelity snapshot where FP8 keeps qualitative metrics within 0.5% of baseline on average, INT8 reduces cost ~45% but had a 1.8% drop on a specific summary metric for prompts with many numeric tables
[04:37] Alicia: numeric tables — yep that's exactly our pain point, lots of lab results and discrete tables in notes, we can't have hallucinated numbers
[04:45] Ethan: then our recommendation is a hybrid: FP8 for the main route; INT8 for short-context prompts where numeric sensitivity is low; plus a sampling rule that escalates prompts with tables to a safer profile. you can mark prompt patterns with regexes or header flags from your app
[05:12] Maya: how invasive is the regex tagging? our app stack is multi-service with a preprocessor, ideally we add a header from the preprocessor to indicate 'TABLE_PRESENT: true'
[05:25] Ethan: that's exactly supported — the router can inspect headers and route accordingly. for private deployments you'd set this as an internal header and the control plane respects it.
[05:39] Raj: what's the cost delta we should expect? rough numbers help procurement — eg cost per 1M tokens for FP8 vs INT8 vs float on your hosted pricing
[05:48] Samira: rough ballpark: float baseline $x per 1M tokens (we'll send exact numbers in the deck), FP8 typically ~40-55% of float cost, INT8 ~25-35% of float cost depending on throughput. important to note quantization isn't free — profiling, evals, and pilot ops have small overheads but pay off fast for high volume
[06:12] Maya: procurement will want an SLA on worst-case latency if we put this in-prod for urgent clinical flows — do you offer latency SLAs for dedicated or private?
[06:22] Ethan: yes, dedicated capacity comes with latency SLOs and contractual SLAs for throughput; private deployment can be configured to meet your internal SLA depending on hardware. our fallbacks also help meet availability SLOs by routing to nearby regions or a higher-tier model if stock kernel isn't available
[06:38] Raj: show me the rollback options in the console please
[06:42] Ethan: demo: Deploy > Rollouts panel, choose route, create canary that uses INT8 profile 10% traffic -> 100% over 24h. You can add automatic health checks: quality regression > 1% revert to previous profile; latency 95th > threshold -> shift to FP8 variant. (console shows thresholds and toggles)
[07:10] [screen share: Optimize console showing rollout config]
[07:25] Alicia: in the health check you mentioned quality regression >1% — is that an absolute metric or relative? we need absolute delta on our key summary metric
[07:34] Ethan: can be either. console accepts both absolute and relative tolerances. you map your ground-truth regression set metric (e.g., ROUGE-L absolute) and set policy to trigger when delta exceeds X points.
[07:47] Raj: can these checks be run on a separate evaluation cluster so we don't consume production tokens?
[07:54] Samira: yes — we recommend a parallel eval runner that uses cached or replicated traffic. it avoids billing production and gives representative checks. also you can do synthetic snapshots from stored prompts in the console
[08:12] Maya: how do we validate hallucination risk specifically for numeric fields? any tooling?
[08:18] Ethan: we have a numeric-field checker in the eval harness — it compares parsed numbers in output to input tables, flags mismatches, and reports per-field precision/recall. this is part of the sandbox metrics and the fidelity snapshot
[08:34] Raj: curious about kernel behaviour — we run long contexts (2k+ tokens). do INT8 kernels support sequence lengths efficiently? i know quant kernels sometimes degrade at long sequences
[08:44] Ethan: great callout — our runtime picks kernels per sequence-length distribution. INT8 kernels can be less stable for very long sequences due to accumulation of quantization error and kv-cache behavior; FP8 has better numerical stability in long-run contexts. we surface expected sensitivity in the kernel recommendations on the profile page
[09:05] [10m of console clicks and brief silence as they look at charts]
[19:20] Samira: jumping back to pilot scope — suggested pilot: 2-week sandbox, 10k prompts from you, compare float vs FP8 vs INT8 with our automated eval suite, run with sampling+rollout rules, and produce a decision report summarizing cost, latency, and fidelity risk.
[19:38] Maya: 2 weeks sounds OK, procurement timeline is about three weeks after pilot sign-off, so we'll need to move quickly if pilot shows acceptable numbers
[19:50] Raj: what telemetry will you provide? we need token-level latency, per-route cost breakdown, per-prompt fidelity flags, and a list of prompts that failed thresholds
[19:59] Ethan: all that is in the Console: token-level heatmaps, route cost breakdown, failure logs, and an exportable CSV of failing prompts with diffs vs baseline. you can hook this into your observability via the tracing hooks or pull via API
[20:20] Alicia: are there examples of customers with clinical data using INT8? we want to know if others successfully rolled out an aggressive quant profile
[20:29] Samira: we've had a couple of health customers use hybrid profiles: FP8 for sensitive routes, INT8 for autocomplete/short prompts. they retained FP8 for table-heavy flows. anonymized case studies in the security deck — i'll share links
[20:45] Maya: security — we'll need SOC2 docs, SSO, SAML, audit logs, and explicit data residency statements; also KMS integration and optional HSM for key material. can you meet that?
[20:57] Ethan: yes — hosted has SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and KMS support; Private install adds HSM options and full control of keys. we can run a security questionnaire. samira will coordinate with your security team
[21:12] Raj: what about offline inference on-prem? do you support air-gapped deployments?
[21:18] Ethan: we have an on-prem package designed for air-gapped installs; control plane can be customer-managed. it requires a bit more upfront ops but meets regulated environments.
[21:28] Maya: what about telemetry — if we're air-gapped we still want evals, how does that work?
[21:35] Ethan: we provide an eval runner that runs locally and emits artifact bundles you can upload to a secure S3 or share via signed link. metrics are produced locally; you choose what to share with Redwood.
[21:50] [short cross talk about procurement dates]
[22:05] Alicia: ok back to cost math — can we see an example decision report? show me the excel/spreadsheet output
[22:12] Ethan: opening example decision report — here's a table: float baseline cost, FP8 cost, INT8 cost, delta, median/95th latency, fidelity metric delta, recommended route. i'll share export after the call
[22:34] Maya: we will want stricter alerts — if any regression on numeric fields appears even at 0.2% we want to halt rollout; can console do a hard stop rather than just notify?
[22:45] Samira: yes, rollout policies can be set to hard-fail and block promotion. the rollback is atomic for that route.
[22:54] Raj: any gotchas on A/B testing vs canary? we want deterministic bucketing because our downstream logging ties back to user ids
[23:02] Ethan: you can control bucketing keys (user id, session id) and use deterministic hashing in the rollout config. That lets you map failures to users and tie back to your logs.
[23:18] Maya: what's your recommended sampling rate for live evals? we don't want to sample too few and miss regressions, but sampling too much costs tokens
[23:27] Ethan: common setup: 0.5%–2% random sampling for broad coverage, and header-driven escalation for known risky flows. For numeric-heavy prompts we push to 10% sampling during canaries.
[23:45] Raj: can we run offline calibration where we sweep bitwidths and top-k/top-p settings together? we have seen interactions between sampling parameters and quantization
[23:55] Ethan: yes — the Optimize sandbox supports multi-axis sweeps: bitwidth, topk/top-p, temperature, and runtime kernel choices. it outputs a multi-dimensional heatmap and CSV.
[24:08] [silence — people typing]
[24:27] Maya: one more question — how quickly can we go from pilot to production if pilot passes? we have a 4-week window ideally
[24:36] Samira: typical timeline: 2-week pilot, 1 week for decision and procurement, 1 week for dedicated capacity provisioning or private install sequencing. 4 weeks is aggressive but achievable if procurement moves fast and we use hosted-dedicated path
[24:52] Alicia: can you send an onboarding checklist so procurement knows the items to approve?
[24:57] Samira: yes, i'll attach the checklist, security pack, and pricing sheet.
[25:06] Raj: let's talk about regressions — what level of manual review do you recommend before cutting over? we want to spot-check a random sample of failing prompts
[25:17] Ethan: recommended practice: automatic gating via rollout policies + manual review queue for failing prompts. the console surfaces a 'needs review' list with highlighted diffs; you can assign owners for triage.
[25:30] Maya: ok good. can your eval harness compute per-field numeric precision easily? we need per-value comparisons because clinicians will reject anything outside tolerance
[25:38] Ethan: yes — you can define structured checks in the eval config for JSON-style outputs or parsed numbers. it reports per-field precision/recall and gives a failing example list.
[25:49] [they briefly discuss JSON-structured extraction for their pipeline]
[26:10] Raj: operationally, if we run a continuous pilot in production traffic for a month, how do we prevent concept drift from eroding the initial results?
[26:19] Ethan: you set periodic snapshot evaluations and rolling re-calibration: weekly automated calibration runs, and alerting if drift metrics cross thresholds. we also recommend keeping a stable holdout set for legal/reg compliance audits
[26:33] Maya: procedural question — for the pilot, who will own the rollback if something breaks in clinical flows? we want a clear oncall contact
[26:41] Samira: we'll assign a Redwood pilot owner (Ethan) and a Nimbus owner (Raj), and we set an oncall escalation matrix in the kickoff. we'll document that in the checklist
[26:55] [longish demo of heatmap export and CSV templates]
[31:10] Samira: wrapping up the demo part — quick checklist of what we'll deliver: pilot access to sandbox, a templated eval config for your summaries, initial microbench logs, and an example rollout policy.
[31:30] Maya: and security docs?
[31:34] Samira: yes security pack attached including SOC2, SAML guide, KMS/HSM options, and an on-prem outline.
[31:42] Alicia: procurement will ask for a price cap if the pilot runs over budget — any suggestions?
[31:48] Samira: we can set a pilot budgeting cap and alerting; also a capped committed usage for the pilot to control costs.
[31:58] Raj: we also need detailed kernel affinity docs — which GPUs and kernels are used per bitwidth and model family, so our infra team can audit compatibility
[32:09] Ethan: will include kernel affinity matrix with the microbench results — that maps model family, bitwidth, sequence length to recommended kernels and expected perf numbers.
[32:22] Maya: fine, thats plenty for now. should we recap next steps?
[32:28] Samira: sure — recap: Samira sends pilot pricing + security pack + checklist; Ethan runs microbench and uploads results; Nimbus provides 10k prompts; schedule 60m sandbox session for next week to go through config and run initial sweep.
[32:44] Maya: sounds good. target dates?
[32:47] Samira: i'll put tentative dates in calendar, aim to start pilot the week of 2025-09-08
[32:54] Raj: timeline noted.
[33:00] [end recap]

Action items (verbatim):
- Samira: share quantization pilot checklist and pricing by 2025-09-02
- Ethan: run INT8/FP8 microbench on 3 model sizes with Nimbus dataset and post by 2025-09-04
- Raj: upload 10k sample prompts + 100 labeled ground-truth completions by 2025-09-01
- Maya: confirm security contacts and send SSO metadata by 2025-09-05

Questions raised:
- How to hard-stop a rollout on numeric field regressions? (Answered: yes, hard-fail policy exists)
- Can offline air-gapped evals be produced and shared? (Answered: yes, artifact bundles)
- How to tag prompts with tables or numeric fields? (Answered: header flags or regexes supported)

End of transcript.
